triage.note: The TOC trap is trap 1 in the sec10k-domain skill and the single most important thing T4 had to survive, but NO committed fixture actually exercises its hard form. In all 11 real HTML/iXBRL fixtures the TOC puts the item code and its title in SEPARATE table cells, so every TOC entry normalizes to a bare 'Item 1.' line with no title -- and the cheap rule 'a real heading carries its title on the same line' kills the entire TOC for free, without the TOC-cluster filter ever running. That left the cluster filter as untested code guarding the repo's most-cited trap. This fixture supplies the missing variant: TOC entries that are single-line and title-bearing, i.e. textually indistinguishable from real body headings (measured: TOC entries score 0.842-0.943 title similarity here, inside the range of genuine headings), so ONLY the cluster rule can separate them.

provenance: SELF-CREATED adversarial fixture: a copy of evals/fixtures/premier-pacific-2016/filing.htm (Premier Pacific Construction, Inc. FY2016 10-K, EDGAR accession 0001127855-17-000104 -- see that fixture's README row for original public-source provenance), mutated 2026-08-16 by one documented, reproducible transformation. THE MUTATION: in the table-of-contents region ONLY -- bounded exactly by the first occurrence of 'ITEM 1.' (the TOC entry, raw offset ~3091 in normalized terms) and the second occurrence of 'ITEM 1.' (the body heading) -- each TOC row's two cells were merged into one by deleting the cell boundary between the code anchor and the title anchor, via the regex '\s*\s*]*>\s*]*>()' -> ' \1'. 43 row boundaries matched and were merged (the TOC has more rows than items because sub-rows and the page-number column participate). File size 642,332 -> 628,096 bytes; the mutation only deletes markup between two anchors, no text content is added, removed, or reordered, and NOTHING outside the TOC region is touched -- the body of the filing is byte-identical to the source fixture. EFFECT, verified after mutation: the pipeline now sees 40 titled candidates scoring at or above the similarity floor where the unmutated fixture yields 20 -- i.e. exactly one extra full set of 20 competing, high-similarity, WRONG candidates, all sitting before the real ones. Sample TOC entries after mutation and their measured title similarity: 'ITEM 1. BUSINESS. 1' (0.842), 'ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS. 2' (0.889), 'ITEM 1B. UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS. 2' (0.943), 'ITEM 4. MINE SAFETY DISCLOSURES. 2' (0.939). Because greedy ordered assignment accepts the EARLIEST surviving candidate for each expected code, a pipeline without a working TOC filter picks the TOC entry for every single item, and every span collapses to a few dozen chars at the top of the document -- the canonical form of this failure, and the reason the domain skill lists it as trap 1. WHY THESE CHECKS: text_contains + min_chars(5000) on Item 1 fail loudly under that failure (under the failure Item 1's span is 21 chars; the real body is 7,496). ANCHOR COUNTS, verified by direct substring count on the mutated fixture's normalized text: 'We were incorporated on March 14, 2012' occurs exactly 2x, once inside Item 1 and once inside Item 7 (the filer repeats the incorporation history in MD&A) -- both occurrences sit deep in body prose, neither is reachable from a TOC-collapsed span, so the anchor discriminates the failure either way. An earlier draft of this case wrote the year as 2013 from memory instead of verifying it against the fixture; the case failed on its own bad anchor while the extraction was correct, and the year was corrected to 2012 (case-authoring step 4 exists precisely for this). 'RISK FACTORS. 2' occurs 1x, only in the mutated TOC and 0x in the unmutated source fixture -- it is a string that exists ONLY because of the mutation, which is what makes it a precise tripwire for TOC bleed. text_not_contains 'RISK FACTORS. 2' catches the specific bleed where Item 1's span starts at the TOC entry and runs on into the next TOC row. Item 9A's real body measures 7,166 chars in both the source and the mutated fixture, so min_chars(1000) on 9A pins a second, independent item deep in the document -- the case cannot pass by getting only the first item right. Finally, item 16 stays 'omitted' per ADR-005 rule 2, unchanged from the source fixture (post-June-2016 filing, no Item 16 heading anywhere). expected_set_complete/only_items assert the same 21-item FY2016 set as premier-pacific-2016-shallow -- the mutation changes markup, never the filing's item inventory. DISCRIMINATION VERIFIED (not merely watched red at NotImplementedError): with the TOC-cluster rule disabled against the finished T4 pipeline this case fails, and with it enabled it passes; the 12 unmutated fixtures are unaffected either way, since their TOCs die at the earlier no-title rule. Tagged 'invariant' because it guards INV-S1/S2 behavior on the trap most likely to silently produce plausible-looking wrong spans.
